rule: Set `team_name` on every Edge3 job row inserted into the database so the fetch endpoint can route jobs and callbacks correctly in multi-team setups
trigger: EdgeJobModel or equivalent job-row insert that omits a `team_name` field inside edge3 executor or callback-handling code
rationale: The fetch endpoint filters on `team_name`; omitting it strands callback jobs or routes them to default-team workers, silently breaking multi-team isolation

evidence.excerpt: fetch endpoint filters on team_name; callback jobs without it get stranded

rule: Do not commit compiled UI `dist/` build artefacts for provider UIs; they must be built by Breeze or at provider-package build time and listed in `.gitignore`
rationale: All other Airflow UI build outputs are gitignored and regenerated during Breeze or provider-package builds; committing dist artefacts pollutes the repo and causes merge conflicts

evidence.excerpt: dist build folder should be gitignored, built by Breeze or provider package

rule: Place Pydantic request/response datamodels for Edge3 worker UI routes in `datamodels_ui.py`, not inline in the route file
trigger: New Pydantic `BaseModel` class defined inside `providers/edge3/.../worker_api/routes/ui.py` instead of in `datamodels_ui.py`
rationale: Consolidating UI datamodels in `datamodels_ui.py` is the established Edge3 provider convention for consistency and discoverability

evidence.excerpt: move this class to datamodels_ui.py for consistency

rule: Use proper HTTP methods for Edge3 UI queue routes: `PUT /worker/{name}/queues` to replace the queue list, not `POST /worker/{name}/queues/add`
trigger: `@ui_router.post` decorator with an action-suffix path like `/queues/add` or `/queues/remove` in edge3 UI routes
rationale: Reviewer asked to leverage REST semantics; `PUT` on the resource URL replaces the queue list, matching how other Airflow REST endpoints are structured

evidence.excerpt: leverage REST call options; use PUT /worker/{name}/queues

rule: Add `testcontainers` as a shared dependency in `devel-common` rather than in individual provider `pyproject.toml` dev-dependency sections
trigger: `testcontainers` added to a `[project.optional-dependencies]` dev block in any provider's `pyproject.toml`
rationale: Multiple providers use testcontainers; centralising it in devel-common avoids version skew and duplication across provider packages

evidence.excerpt: move testcontainers to devel-common; second provider using it now

rule: Guard Airflow-2 log-upload code paths in providers with `if not AIRFLOW_V_3_0_PLUS` rather than deleting them, so the provider continues to work against Airflow 2
trigger: Deletion of a log-upload or logging-handler code path in a provider that previously supported Airflow 2, without an `AIRFLOW_V_3_0_PLUS` guard
rationale: Providers must remain compatible with both Airflow 2 and 3; removing Airflow-2 paths without version guards silently breaks users on Airflow 2

evidence.excerpt: need AIRFLOW_V_3_0_PLUS guard; Airflow 2 still needs log upload path

rule: Use the existing `_build_es_search_response()` test helper to construct Elasticsearch response fixtures instead of hand-rolling response dicts
trigger: Hand-rolled ES response dict (e.g. `{"hits": {"total": ..., "hits": []}}`) used as a mock return value in elasticsearch provider tests
rationale: Hand-rolled dicts drift from the schema `ElasticSearchResponse` expects; the shared helper produces a fully-shaped, consistent fixture that guards against regressions

evidence.excerpt: use _build_es_search_response() helper for fully-shaped, resilient fixture

rule: Name FastAPI request/response datamodel classes `*Body` and `*Response`, not `*In` and `*Out`, to match the Airflow Core API naming convention
trigger: Pydantic model class name ending in `In` or `Out` (e.g. `RoleIn`, `RoleOut`) in any Airflow FastAPI datamodels file
rationale: The Airflow Core API uses `*Body`/`*Response` convention; FAB and other providers must follow the same pattern for consistency across the codebase

evidence.excerpt: use Body and Response not In and Out; that's the convention in other APIs

rule: Import FastAPI utilities from `fastapi`, not directly from `starlette`, in provider route files
trigger: `from starlette.exceptions import HTTPException` or `from starlette import status` in a provider FastAPI route or dependency file
rationale: Repo-wide convention is to use `fastapi` imports; direct `starlette` imports are being replaced across the codebase via follow-up PRs

evidence.excerpt: replace from-starlette imports; follow-up PRs aligning across codebase

rule: Place FAB authorization helper functions (e.g. `requires_fab_custom_view`) in the service module, not in the route module, to mirror Airflow Core API conventions
trigger: Authorization dependency function defined inside a `routes/*.py` file rather than the corresponding `services/*.py` file in the FAB provider
rationale: Airflow Core API keeps authorization helpers in service modules; FAB provider routes must follow the same layering convention

evidence.excerpt: move requires_fab_custom_view to service module; Airflow Core follows this

rule: Do not describe `order_by` parameters as accepting comma-separated fields if the underlying `build_ordering()` helper only supports a single field
trigger: `order_by` query-parameter description containing "comma" or "separated by comma" in a route that calls `build_ordering()` with a single field
rationale: `build_ordering()` only handles one field; claiming multi-field support misleads callers and causes silent 400 errors for valid-looking requests

evidence.excerpt: build_ordering() supports only one field; comma-separated description misleads callers

rule: Use `get_fab_auth_manager()` (or an `isinstance` check) instead of `cast(FabAuthManager, get_auth_manager())` to retrieve the FAB auth manager, and raise a clear exception when it is not configured
trigger: `cast("FabAuthManager", get_auth_manager())` or `cast(FabAuthManager, get_auth_manager())` in FAB provider route or helper code
rationale: A bare `cast` masks misconfiguration; when OpenAPI generation runs with a different auth manager configured it produces a silent `AttributeError` instead of an actionable error

evidence.excerpt: cast masks misconfiguration; use get_fab_auth_manager() or isinstance check

rule: When dropping Edge3 ORM tables programmatically, pass `Model.__tablename__` (the string table name) rather than `Model.__table__` (the Table object) to the drop call
trigger: Reference to `EdgeWorkerModel.__table__`, `EdgeJobModel.__table__`, or `EdgeLogsModel.__table__` in a drop-table list or `Base.metadata.remove()` call
rationale: SQLAlchemy drop APIs expect the string table name; using `.__table__` passes the mapped Table object and is the wrong type for the intended operation

evidence.excerpt: use __tablename__ not __table__ for the drop list
